title: Why More Context Makes Your Agent Dumber and What to Do About It — Nupur Sharma, Qodo

summary: Nupur Sharma, working at Qodo on agentic code reviews, brings a dev-sec-ops background where pipelines were deterministic and contrasts it with the non-deterministic world of agents. She traces agent evolution from static 4K context prompts, to agentic workflows with search tools that created looping behavior, to multi-agent architectures where tool proliferation causes understanding clashes between agents. The central insight is the U curve: when given large context, LLMs focus on initial and final inputs while purging middle context. Qodo benchmarks this by giving agents full codebases and observing that mid-context items like Jira tickets and MCPs get dropped. Growing context windows alone does not solve this. She presents five context optimization strategies with tradeoffs: context engines (scaling challenges at 600-700 repos), hierarchical summarization (high ongoing LLM cost), knowledge graphs (high upfront effort), iterative retrieval (low dev input, recommended for non-product companies), and self-correction with a critic node (added latency, low upfront input). The orchestration paradox describes how increasingly smart LLMs waste API tokens researching methods rather than solving problems. Qodo's fix is an 80/20 hybrid: 80% uses high-reasoning models for open-ended discovery; 20% uses deterministic models for validation. Guardrails like iteration counters (4-5) and timeouts (5 minutes) prevent infinite loops. Single agents given multiple tasks lose focus, motivating a mixture of specialized agents. Qodo's code review architecture implements this: a context collector gathers context from PRs, the context engine, and tools, then bifurcates relevant context to specialized agents (security, code differences, Jira issues). A judge agent recombines their results, checks relevance against PR history and organizational guidelines, and can revisit the context engine to refine recommendations. Built on LangChain, agents communicate by collecting results and crafting refined prompts for the next agent. Calibration happens through PR history indexing and a compliance portal where architects and compliance teams upload guidelines. Every accepted suggestion increases its weight for future runs; rejected suggestions decrease. Rules (e.g., no hardcoded API keys) are always highlighted regardless of developer preference, while repeated rejections of bug suggestions reduce their future weight.

sections.title: Introduction and Agent Evolution
sections.summary: Nupur introduces her background in deterministic dev-sec-ops and transition to non-deterministic agents at Qodo. She traces agent evolution from static 4K context prompts, to agentic workflows with search tools that create loops, to multi-agent architectures where tool proliferation causes understanding clashes.

sections.title: The U Curve Problem
sections.summary: Explains the U curve: LLMs focus on initial and final context inputs while purging the middle. Qodo benchmarks this by providing full codebases and observing that mid-context items like Jira tickets and MCPs get dropped. Growing context windows alone does not fix this.

sections.title: Context Optimization Strategies
sections.summary: Covers five strategies with tradeoffs: context engines (bouncer metaphor, scaling issues at 600+ repos), hierarchical summarization (high ongoing LLM cost), knowledge graphs (high upfront effort, good for dependencies), iterative retrieval (low dev input, recommended for non-product companies), and self-correction with critic node (added latency, low upfront input).

sections.title: Orchestration Paradox and 80/20 Hybrid Approach
sections.summary: Describes how smart LLMs waste tokens researching methods rather than solving problems. Qodo's 80/20 hybrid gives high-reasoning models 80% for open-ended discovery and deterministic models 20% for validation. Guardrails like iteration counters (4-5) and timeouts (5 minutes) prevent infinite loops.

sections.title: Mixture of Agents and Judge Agent Concept
sections.summary: Addresses single-agent overload where multiple tasks cause focus loss on some tasks. Proposes mixture of specialized issue-expert agents instead. Uses vacation planning example to show how independent agents produce mismatched results, motivating the judge agent concept for recombination.

sections.title: Qodo's Code Review Architecture and Calibration
sections.summary: Details Qodo's live architecture: a context collector gathers context from PRs, the context engine, and tools, then bifurcates relevant context to specialized agents (security, code differences, Jira issues). A judge agent recombines results, checks relevance against PR history and organizational guidelines, and refines recommendations. Built on LangChain, agents communicate via collected results turned into refined prompts. Calibration uses PR history indexing and a compliance portal where architects and compliance teams upload guidelines. Every accepted suggestion increases weight for future runs; rejected suggestions decrease. Rules are always highlighted regardless of developer preference, while repeated rejections of bug suggestions reduce their future weight.

demonstrations: Qodo benchmarks agents by providing full codebase context and observing which parts are retained vs. purged

limitations: Context engines: indexing takes moderate effort, scaling to hundreds of repos is unpredictable
Hierarchical summarization: requires high ongoing LLM processing for every file change
Knowledge graphs: complex, high upfront developer input, time-consuming to create
Self-correction: adds latency from re-running agents
Single agents with multiple tasks lose focus on some tasks
High-reasoning models are unnecessary for deterministic validation tasks
Specialized agents lack the full picture, which may limit architectural or cross-cutting decisions
PR history as a calibration source does not guarantee quality since past patterns may not be good practices
Without organizational guidelines, agents cannot surface domain-specific issues
